newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia oil chief says Corporo-1 unworkable.
newsitem.headline: Colombia oil chief says Corporo-1 unworkable.

text.p: BOGOTA, May 5 Reuter - The head of Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol said Monday that definitive studies showed that crude cannot be extracted from the much-vaunted Corporo-1 well -- ending months of speculation over the future of the prospect.

But in a statement, Antonio Jose Urdinola said geological data gleaned about Corporo would be used to help draw up a detailed geological evaluation of the rest of the so-called Medina block, on the edge of the eastern plains.
A decision on whether to sink wells elsewhere in the block would be taken by mid-year, he said.
"Tests showed that hydrocarbons occupy an important portion of the porous area but they are not extractable because of the low porosity and the low permeability of the rocks," Urdinola said.

In September last year, the Colombian government forecast Corporo could prove to be one of the country's largest oil funds to date and forecast reserves of between 700,000 and 1.3 billion barrels of crude.
Ecopetrol experts then dented hopes, citing notoriously difficult drilling conditions and low rock porosity in this region of Colombia.

But Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar revived the debate on a trip to the United States earlier this year, estimating reserves of up to 3 billion barrels adding that there was a 17 percent chance of being able to extract the crude -- about average for this area.
Ecopetrol spent $60.5 million in studies and test drills in Corporo.
